speaker: Attorney
text: All right. I want to shift now from the car to the truck. Is that okay with you?

speaker: Witness B
text: That's fine.

speaker: Attorney
text: At some point that afternoon, before the crash, did you notice a large truck near the intersection?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. A big white truck. A tractor with a long trailer behind it.

speaker: Attorney
text: Do you remember when you first noticed it?

speaker: Witness B
text: Not to the minute. It was a little while before everything happened. I just noticed it sitting over there on the other side.

speaker: Attorney
text: When you say the other side, what do you mean?

speaker: Witness B
text: The westbound side. Across the median from the store. The lanes going the other direction, toward town.

speaker: Attorney
text: Was it in one of the westbound travel lanes, or somewhere else?

speaker: Witness B
text: It was in the turn lane. The little left-turn lane they have there for the crossover.

speaker: Attorney
text: Just so the record is clear, that's the turn lane on the westbound side that lets you turn left across the median toward 140th?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. That one.

speaker: Attorney
text: How did you know it was in the turn lane and not the regular lane?

speaker: Witness B
text: Because it was over on the left, by the median, where the lane cuts in. The regular lanes were to the right of it, and cars were going by it in those.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you see cars going by it in the westbound lanes?

speaker: Witness B
text: A couple, I think. Not a lot. It wasn't busy.

speaker: Attorney
text: Tell me what you remember about the truck itself. Start with the trailer.

speaker: Witness B
text: The trailer was white. Long. A box trailer, all closed in. Like a big metal box on wheels.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you notice anything on the front of the trailer?

speaker: Witness B
text: There was a unit up on the front of it, up high, behind the cab. A refrigeration thing, I'd guess. I could hear it running.

speaker: Attorney
text: What did it sound like?

speaker: Witness B
text: A hum. Kind of a steady hum, like a big air conditioner. You hear them at truck stops.

speaker: Attorney
text: Could you hear that hum from where you were outside the store?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form.

speaker: Attorney
text: You can answer.

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. Once things got quiet between cars, you could hear it. It's a constant sound.

speaker: Attorney
text: What about the cab, the tractor part. What do you remember about that?

speaker: Witness B
text: It was darker than the trailer. I don't remember the exact color. A regular big rig cab. Not one of the flat-front ones, it had a hood.

speaker: Attorney
text: Do you have any estimate of how long the trailer was?

speaker: Witness B
text: Long. The regular long kind. I couldn't give you feet. I'm not good with distances, I said that before.

speaker: Attorney
text: That's fine. Would you say it was the size of trailer you typically see on the highway, the big ones?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form. Leading.

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes, the big ones. Not a short one. The full size.

speaker: Attorney
text: When you first noticed the truck in the turn lane, was it stopped, or was it moving?

speaker: Witness B
text: I really can't tell you for sure. It was either stopped or just barely rolling. Creeping, maybe.

speaker: Attorney
text: What makes you say it might have been creeping?

speaker: Witness B
text: It just didn't seem totally still to me. But I wasn't staring at it. It could have been stopped. I don't want to say one way or the other.

speaker: Attorney
text: I understand. I don't want you to guess. Is it fair to say you don't know whether it was stopped or creeping?

speaker: Witness B
text: That's fair. It was one or the other. Sitting there or close to it.

speaker: Attorney
text: Do you know how long it was in the turn lane before it began its turn?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. It was there when I noticed it. I don't know how long it had been there.

speaker: Attorney
text: Were there any other vehicles in that turn lane, in front of it or behind it?

speaker: Witness B
text: Not that I remember. Just the truck.

speaker: Attorney
text: Okay. At some point did the truck begin to turn?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes.

speaker: Attorney
text: Describe for me what you saw it do.

speaker: Witness B
text: It started coming across. It pulled out of the turn lane, into the crossover, the gap in the median, and then the front of it started across the eastbound lanes. Toward our side. Toward 140th.

speaker: Attorney
text: When you say our side, you mean the south side of the highway, the side the store is on?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. The store side.

speaker: Attorney
text: Which part of the truck came across first?

speaker: Witness B
text: The cab. The front. Then the trailer follows behind it, the way they do. It kind of swings around.

speaker: Attorney
text: Describe the path of the cab, as best you can.

speaker: Witness B
text: It came out of the median and angled across, toward the side road. Heading for 140th. It was turning left, so it was curving toward my left as I looked at it. Toward the south.

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form.

speaker: Attorney
text: I'll rephrase. From where you were, which way did the cab appear to be heading as it crossed?

speaker: Witness B
text: Toward 140th. Toward the side road that goes down past the store.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did it appear to you to be making a normal left turn into 140th?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form. Foundation.

speaker: Attorney
text: If you can answer.

speaker: Witness B
text: It looked like a regular left turn to me. It was going where the road goes. I'm not an expert in trucks.

speaker: Attorney
text: How fast was the truck moving as it turned?

speaker: Witness B
text: Slow.

speaker: Attorney
text: Can you give me any sense of how slow?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form.

speaker: Witness B
text: Slow like a big truck turning. A little faster than somebody walking, maybe. Not much. They don't go fast when they're turning like that.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did the speed change as it went through the turn?

speaker: Witness B
text: Not that I could tell. It was kind of steady. Slow and steady. Maybe it picked up a little once it was moving. I really don't know.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you see it stop at any point during the turn, before the crash?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. I didn't see it stop. Once it started across, it kept going.

speaker: Attorney
text: How long, from when it started moving out of the turn lane, did the turn take?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form.

speaker: Witness B
text: A few seconds. I don't know. It felt slow. It wasn't like a car whipping across. It took its time.

speaker: Attorney
text: When you say a few seconds, are you able to put any number on that?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. I'd be making it up. Several seconds. It was slow. That's all I can tell you.

speaker: Attorney
text: I'm not asking you to make anything up. If you don't know, that's a fine answer.

speaker: Witness B
text: Then I don't know the exact number. It was a few seconds, and it was slow.

speaker: Attorney
text: As the truck turned, did you hear anything from it?

speaker: Witness B
text: The engine. You could hear the engine working, like a low rumble when they pull out. And that hum from the trailer.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did the engine noise change during the turn?

speaker: Witness B
text: It got a little louder when it started pulling. Then it was just steady. Like a big diesel. That's all I remember.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you hear the truck's horn at any point?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. I don't remember any horn.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you hear any air brakes, that hiss trucks make?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. I didn't hear brakes. Not from the truck, not from anybody.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you hear any other sounds from the truck, any squeal, anything like that?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. Just the engine and the hum.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you notice whether the truck had any lights on?

speaker: Witness B
text: I didn't notice lights. It was broad daylight. I wasn't looking for that.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you notice a turn signal on the truck?

speaker: Witness B
text: I don't remember. I didn't notice it either way. I'm not saying it was or wasn't on.

speaker: Attorney
text: Understood. Now, as the truck came across the eastbound lanes, where did the trailer end up relative to those lanes?

speaker: Witness B
text: Across them. The trailer was stretched across the road. Both eastbound lanes.

speaker: Attorney
text: Both lanes?

speaker: Witness B
text: Both. The inside lane and the outside lane. It was long enough that it covered the whole thing, more or less.

speaker: Attorney
text: When you say covered, do you mean the trailer was across both of the eastbound lanes at the same moment?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. At one point it was across both of them. The cab was over toward 140th and the trailer was back across the road behind it.

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form.

speaker: Attorney
text: Let me break that down. At the moment the trailer was across both lanes, where was the cab?

speaker: Witness B
text: The cab was mostly across already. Up near the edge of the road on our side, starting into 140th, or close to it.

speaker: Attorney
text: And the back of the trailer, where was that?

speaker: Witness B
text: Still back in the median area, I think. Back toward where it came from. The back wheels were still coming through the crossover.

speaker: Attorney
text: Are you confident about where the back of the trailer was?

speaker: Witness B
text: Not exactly confident. It was back there somewhere. In the median or right near it. I wasn't looking at the back wheels.

speaker: Attorney
text: Okay. Was the trailer moving or stopped when it was across both lanes?

speaker: Witness B
text: Moving. Slow, still moving. It was still turning.

speaker: Attorney
text: Was the trailer straight across the road, or at an angle?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form.

speaker: Witness B
text: At an angle, I'd say. Because it was still bending around the turn. Not straight across like a wall, more slanted.

speaker: Attorney
text: Slanted in which direction, if you can say?

speaker: Witness B
text: I can't really say better than that. It was angled. The front was ahead of the back. That's how they turn.

speaker: Attorney
text: Fair enough. Which side of the trailer was facing the oncoming eastbound traffic?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form. Foundation.

speaker: Attorney
text: If you know.

speaker: Witness B
text: The side of it. The long side. Coming from the west you'd be looking at the long side. The right side of it, I guess, if you're the truck.

speaker: Attorney
text: Okay. Let me go back a step. When the truck started its turn, where was the car, if you know?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form.

speaker: Witness B
text: Coming down the hill. Coming east. It had already come over the top, I think, when the truck started moving.

speaker: Attorney
text: You think, or you know?

speaker: Witness B
text: I think. I believe the car was already over the hill when the truck pulled out. That's how I remember it. But I wouldn't swear to the second.

speaker: Attorney
text: In your earlier testimony this morning you said you first noticed the car as it came over the hill. Was the truck still in the turn lane at that moment?

speaker: Witness B
text: I think it was still in the turn lane, or just starting. It started across after, or about the same time. Not long after.

speaker: Attorney
text: So the sequence you recall is the car comes over the hill, and then the truck begins across, or about the same time?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form. Asked and answered.

speaker: Attorney
text: You can answer.

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. That's my memory. Car over the hill, truck starts across, about together or right after.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you see the truck at any point stop, back up, or pause once it was in the eastbound lanes?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. It kept coming across.

speaker: Attorney
text: Were there any other eastbound vehicles anywhere near the intersection while the truck was turning?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. Just the car. I don't remember anybody else coming east right then.

speaker: Attorney
text: And westbound, while the truck was turning?

speaker: Witness B
text: I think a car went by westbound, maybe one. I really don't remember for sure. It was quiet.

speaker: Attorney
text: Let's talk about the car's position relative to the truck. As the truck moved across, which lane was the car in?

speaker: Witness B
text: The right lane. The outside one, nearest the store. Like I said before.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did the car stay in that lane while the truck was turning?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. It stayed right there. Straight.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you see the car move toward the left lane, or toward the shoulder, at any point while the truck was crossing?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. It didn't move over. It just kept straight in its lane.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did the car appear to you to slow down as the truck crossed in front of it?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form. Foundation.

speaker: Attorney
text: I'm asking only what you saw.

speaker: Witness B
text: I didn't see it slow down. It kept coming the same as it was. I didn't see any change.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you hear any braking from the car? Tires, anything?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. No tires, no squealing. Nothing until the crash itself.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you hear a horn from the car?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. No horn from anybody.

speaker: Attorney
text: Now, I'm going to ask you about the last moment before the impact, but I'm not going to ask you yet about the impact itself. We'll get there. Okay?

speaker: Witness B
text: Okay.

speaker: Attorney
text: Just before the impact, where was the truck?

speaker: Witness B
text: Across the road. The cab was over on our side, heading into 140th, and the trailer was across the eastbound lanes.

speaker: Attorney
text: Was the truck still moving at that moment?

speaker: Witness B
text: I think so. Still slow. Still going.

speaker: Attorney
text: And the car, just before the impact, where was it?

speaker: Witness B
text: Right there. In the right lane, coming up to the trailer.

speaker: Attorney
text: Which part of the truck did the car come up on? The cab, the trailer?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form.

speaker: Witness B
text: The trailer. The side of the trailer. Not the cab. The cab was already past.

speaker: Attorney
text: Do you know about where along the trailer? Front, middle, back?

speaker: Witness B
text: Somewhere in the middle, more toward the back maybe. Behind the cab, ahead of the back wheels. I couldn't tell you exactly.

speaker: Attorney
text: Okay. We'll come back to that. I want to ask a few more general things about the truck. Had you seen that truck before that day, at the store or on the road?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. Not that I know of. Lots of trucks go through there. I wouldn't know one from another.

speaker: Attorney
text: Going back to that afternoon. While the truck was in the turn lane, before it started across, did you see anything about the truck that seemed unusual to you?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form.

speaker: Witness B
text: No. It was just a truck waiting to turn. Nothing stood out. I didn't think anything of it.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you see any doors open on it, anything loose, anything like that?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. Nothing like that.

speaker: Attorney
text: Okay. Did the trailer at any point cross into the area of 140th itself, before the crash?

speaker: Witness B
text: The front part of the truck was going into 140th. The trailer was still mostly on the highway when it happened.

speaker: Attorney
text: How much of the truck, if any, was on 140th at the moment of the crash, if you can say?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form.

speaker: Witness B
text: The cab, maybe. Starting onto it. Maybe a little of the front of the trailer. I can't say exactly.

speaker: Attorney
text: Okay. Let me ask it this way. Was the cab on the highway or past the highway when the crash happened?

speaker: Witness B
text: At the edge, or just past it. Going onto 140th. It was most of the way through the turn with the front end.

speaker: Attorney
text: And you're describing the cab's position there based on what you saw at the time?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. Based on what I saw.

speaker: Attorney
text: Okay. One moment.

speaker: Attorney
text: I want to make sure I have the timeline straight. You noticed the truck sitting in the westbound turn lane, stopped or creeping, correct?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes.

speaker: Attorney
text: You don't know how long it had been there?

speaker: Witness B
text: No.

speaker: Attorney
text: At about the time the car came over the hill, the truck began its turn?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form. Mischaracterizes.

speaker: Attorney
text: Is that a fair summary of what you said?

speaker: Witness B
text: About that time, or right after. Yes.

speaker: Attorney
text: The truck moved out of the turn lane, through the crossover, and across the eastbound lanes, toward 140th?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes.

speaker: Attorney
text: Slowly?

speaker: Witness B
text: Slowly.

speaker: Attorney
text: Without stopping, that you saw?

speaker: Witness B
text: Without stopping that I saw.

speaker: Attorney
text: And at some point the trailer was across both eastbound lanes?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. Both of them.

speaker: Attorney
text: And during that time, you didn't hear a horn and you didn't hear brakes?

speaker: Witness B
text: No horn. No brakes. Just the engine and the hum.

speaker: Attorney
text: Is there anything about the truck's movements that you remember that I haven't asked you about?

speaker: Witness B
text: I don't think so. That's what I remember. It came across slow, and the trailer was across the road.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you say anything out loud, or call out, while the truck was turning?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. There wasn't time to say anything, and I don't know who I would have said it to. I was just standing there.

speaker: Attorney
text: Was anyone else outside the store with you during the truck's turn?

speaker: Witness B
text: Not right with me. I don't remember anybody else outside right then. The girl who worked there was inside.

speaker: Attorney
text: How do you know she was inside?

speaker: Witness B
text: Because she came out after. After the crash. She came out the door.

speaker: Attorney
text: We'll get to that. Before the crash, did you see anyone else on the store property, in the lot?

speaker: Witness B
text: There might have been a car parked. I don't remember people. It was quiet.

speaker: Attorney
text: Just a few more about the truck. After the truck got across, and we'll talk about this more later, did you see where it ended up?

speaker: Witness B
text: It went on down 140th. It kept going a ways and stopped down there past the store.

speaker: Attorney
text: We'll come back to exactly where. Did it stop right away, or keep going?

speaker: Witness B
text: It kept going a little. It didn't stop right at the highway. It went down some and then stopped.

speaker: Attorney
text: Okay. We'll pick that up later this morning. I'm going to move now to the moment of impact, which is the next area.
